question.text: Which of the following entities is NOT eligible to be a promoter of a Credit Rating Agency as per SEBI (Credit Rating Agencies) Regulations, 1999?

answer.text: A scheduled commercial bank included in the Second Schedule to the RBI Act, 1934
A foreign credit rating agency incorporated in a FATF member jurisdiction, recognized under the laws of that jurisdiction, with at least five years of experience in rating securities
A company with a net worth of Rs. 50 crore continuously for the previous five years
A public financial institution as defined in section 2(72) of Companies Act, 2013

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI (CRA) Regulations, 1999 require a company/body corporate promoter of a CRA to have a continuous net worth of at least Rs. 100 crore for the previous five years. A company with only Rs. 50 crore net worth fails this threshold and is therefore not eligible. The other three options - a Second-Schedule scheduled commercial bank, a public financial institution under s.2(72) of the Companies Act 2013, and a foreign CRA incorporated in a FATF member jurisdiction, recognized under that jurisdiction's law, and with at least five years' rating experience - each meet a category-specific eligibility limb. The Trap: Rs. 50 crore looks substantial but falls short of the Rs. 100 crore requirement. In the original ambiguous wording, option B only mentioned five years' rating experience without the FATF/recognition limbs, which made it look incomplete and potentially also ineligible. Note: The original question was ambiguous because option B did not specify the FATF member jurisdiction and recognition-under-local-law conditions required by p.385 of NISM-Series-III-A (Securities Intermediaries Compliance Non-Fund, Dec 2025). Option B has been tightened to include those conditions so that only option C is uniquely ineligible.
